Panel: STANFILL, C.J., and MEAD, CONNORS, LAWRENCE, DOUGLAS, and LIPEZ, JJ.
ASHLEY LYNNE
v.
DEPARTMENT OF HEALTH AND HUMAN SERVICES et al.
CONNORS, J. [¶1] When MaineCare pays the costs of medical treatment of an injury for which a third party is liable and the MaineCare recipient settles a tort claim with the third party, the Department of Health and Human Services may recover “the cost of benefits provided” by MaineCare, but only “to the extent of the recovery for medical expenses.” 22 M.R.S. § 14(1) (2026) . The question presented in this appeal is how to determine the extent to which a recipient has recovered for medical expenses, and, thus, the upper limit of the Department’s reimbursement, when a settlement between the recipient and the third party does not allocate damages between medical expenses and other damages. In this action between a recipient and the Department to determine the amount that the Department may recover , the Superior Court (Androscoggin County, 2 Archer, J.) entered summary judgment in favor of the recipient. We conclude that in order to allocate this settlement, the court must resolve disputed factual issues, and so we vacate and remand for further proceedings. I. item.title: New counsel memo: Standard of review for Right-to-Sue requests made before 180 days have passed
item.description:
MEMO TO: Kit Thomson Crossman, Executive Director FROM: Barbara Archer Hirsch, Commission Counsel Colin R. Hurd, Deputy Commission Counsel DATE: July 23, 2025 RE: Standard of review for right-to-sue requests made before 180 days have passed As you are aware, 5 M.R.S. § 4612(6)(B), enacted in 2023, delineates the circumstances in which the Executive Director (“ED”) shall issue a right-to-sue letter (“RTS”) to a complainant who requests one before their complaint has aged 180 days with the Commission. Prior to the 2023 enactment, complainants could never request an RTS prior to 180 days. Now, the Commission “shall” issue an early RTS when two elements are concurrently met. First, the ED must determine that the complainant demonstrated good cause for requesting the RTS before the passage of 180 days, and second, the ED must certify that it is probable that the Commission will be unable to conclude its investigation before the 180 th day from the date on which the complaint was filed. After 180 days have passed, the complainant may request and receive an RTS without having to meet these standards. The second element of § 4612(6)(B) is relatively straightforward. The first element, however, is more nuanced. The Maine Human Rights Act does not define “good cause”. The Commission’s Procedural Rule provides that the Commission may grant extensions of certain time limits “for good cause shown”, 94-348 C.M.R. Ch. 2, § 2.11(C), but also do not define the term. In practice, the Commission requires that parties seeking extensions demonstrate that the requested extension is necessary due to extenuating circumstances, such as serious personal illness or a death in the family; inconvenience is insufficient to meet this standard.

Looking Ahead: Eligibility-Dedicated Data Feed to Support MaineCare Renewals and Enrollment

Sep 04, 2026

Two weeks ago, we announced communications support for MaineCare partners and providers regarding changes the federal government is making to MaineCare (Maine’s Medicaid program) eligibility. This message provides an early look at planned data-sharing that will help the Maine Department of Health and Human Services (DHHS) verify information needed for MaineCare eligibility. Our goal is to help eligible Mainers keep their coverage and access to services with as little disruption as possible.

No action is needed now. We are sharing this information early to make providers aware of what is being planned. We will share more information as plans and timelines are finalized.

DHHS will continue to use administrative data sources it has access to as much as possible to support automatic (“passive”) renewals for MaineCare members. Federal changes to eligibility mean we need additional information to help more eligible members maintain their MaineCare coverage. This data will help Mainers continue to benefit from MaineCare, which in turn will help providers minimize the impact of these federal Medicaid cuts on their revenue and on their charity and uncompensated care.

Clinical Data Will Help People Stay Enrolled in MaineCare

Electronic health record (EHR) systems contain clinical data that Maine and numerous other states are planning to use to help exempt Medicaid applicants and members with work-limiting health conditions from Work Requirements. In Maine, this data will support MaineCare eligibility determination activities administered by the Office for Family Independence (OFI). DHHS intends to partner with providers to collect this information through HealthInfoNet, the State’s contractor for this work. HealthInfoNet will identify indicators of exemptions from work requirements by collecting and processing this clinical data from providers. Using clinical data alongside claims and other administrative data to generate more timely and comprehensive information will help keep Mainers enrolled in MaineCare. We will refer to the data sent to HealthInfoNet for this purpose as the eligibility-dedicated clinical data feed.

Until the eligibility-dedicated clinical data feed is established we will be basing automatic exceptions for work-limiting health conditions on claims data alone in order to meet implementation deadlines.

This Data Sharing Will Be Separate from the Health Information Exchange

The eligibility-dedicated clinical data feed will be separate from the health information exchange (HIE) data that many providers already share with HealthInfoNet.

The eligibility-dedicated data feed will include only the information needed to support MaineCare eligibility activities. This information will be stored separately from HIE data. It will not be available through HealthInfoNet’s clinical portal or through analytics tools used by some provider organizations. The eligibility-dedicated clinical data feed will be used only in support of OMS and OFI activities associated with eligibility.

Key details to note:

  • The steps needed for a provider to establish this new data feed will vary by provider organization. For example, some provider organizations already have a data feed with HealthInfoNet that can be used as a starting point. Capabilities of the organization’s EHR vendor or technology support may also affect the work needed to establish the data feed. Providers eligible for relevant Rural Health Transformation Program (RHTP) funding may consider using this funding for these costs, as determined by the allowable uses of specific RHTP opportunities.
  • We expect it will take the majority of provider organizations two to four months to build their eligibility-dedicated clinical data feed with HealthInfoNet. This time range will be dependent on provider organization’s or vendor’s availability to engage with HealthInfoNet. We expect it will take less time than building a typical HIE data sharing connection with HealthInfoNet.
  • Clinical care teams are not expected to need to take additional steps to send this information as part of their day-to-day work. Once the data feed is established, the identified data categories will be shared automatically with HealthInfoNet.
  • Broad categories of exemptions in statute for work-limiting health conditions include those who are blind or disabled, have a substance use disorder, disabling mental disorder, or complex medical condition. DHHS continues to work with the federal government to clarify data related to these categories that may assist states to automatically exempt individuals, including information related to a person’s ability to work. Kinds of data may include demographic information, diagnosis indicators, encounter or event indicators, and billing codes, among others.

More Information Will Be Coming – No Action Needed Now The Department and HealthInfoNet will distribute instructions for provider organizations to opt into this initiative and implement the eligibility-dedicated data feed. Future communications will include information such as:

  • Which provider types will be prioritized for establishing these connections
  • How providers can participate
  • The types of information that will be needed
  • Technical requirements and specifications
  • Onboarding and implementation steps
  • Timelines

Attention Trading Partners: Training for New MaineCare Partner Portal

Sep 08, 2026

We have previously shared that a refreshed and upgraded MIHMS, with a new “MaineCare Partner Portal,” is coming in October 2026. This will replace the current HealthPAS Online Portal. We are now inviting trading partners to register for training that begins September 8, 2026 to help you prepare for the transition to the new portal. Trading partners include providers, billing agents, health plans, clearinghouses, and business associates. Trading partners have an important role to play in supporting a smooth transition and uninterrupted access to the portal after go-live. 

Gainwell Technologies will be leading live virtual instructor-led training sessions. These courses will provide the knowledge and skills needed to navigate the new portal, complete daily business functions, and use new portal features. Training demonstrations, materials, and supporting resources will help participants prepare for a successful transition. 

Steps you need to take to attend training 

  • Review the available training topics listed below and identify the sessions that align with your role and responsibilities. 
  • Use the LMS registration (instructions below) to create an account, access the training catalog, and enroll in applicable sessions. 
  • Contact Gainwell (instructions below) if you need assistance. 
  • Recorded sessions and other training materials will be available in the LMS after training sessions for ongoing reference. 

MaineCare Partner Portal Training Sessions 

Course Name 

Description 

ME - TPT - Migrated Trading Partner Log In and Account Maintenance Training (ILC) 

Learn how to complete first-time login activities, configure multi-factor authentication (MFA), manage user accounts and permissions, perform account maintenance activities, and understand electronic data interchange (EDI) certification requirements and status monitoring. This course is only for Admin (R7) users. 

ME - TPT - Trading Partner Registration and Account Maintenance Training (ILC) 

Learn how to register a new Trading Partner account, complete account activation, manage users and permissions, associate providers and billing agents, navigate the portal, and maintain account information.  

ME - TPT - Authorization, Referrals and Certifications Training (ILC) 

Learn how to submit and manage authorizations, process referrals, monitor certification requests and statuses, and access related portal functionality. 

ME - TPT - Dental Claim Entry & Claim Management Training (ILC) 

Learn how to submit dental claims, monitor claim processing and status, and navigate claim-related portal functions. 

ME - TPT - Institutional Claim Entry & Claim Management Training (ILC) 

Learn how to submit institutional claims, monitor claim processing and status, and navigate claim-related portal functions. 

ME - TPT - Professional Claim Entry & Claim Management Training (ILC) 

Learn how to submit professional claims, monitor claim status, review payment information, access remittance advice, and complete related claim activities. 

ME - TPT - MaineCare Partner Public Portal Training (ILC) 

Learn about publicly available portal functionality, portal resources and reference materials, secure messaging, Trading Partner tools, and available resources. 

LMS Access and Course Registration Instructions 

Use the following steps to register for MaineCare Partner Portal training. Multiple sessions are available for each course to allow for scheduling flexibility. 

  1. Go to the LMS registration site: https://mmislearningcenter.myabsorb.com/#/login. 
  2. Sign in using your existing account or click Sign Up on the right side of the window to create a new account. 
  3. If you need a new account, enter the enrollment key: De8pO9CBYXYB-aOCY8qp on the Sign Up window. 
  4. Complete the required registration information to create your account. Note: You can enter your workplace address. 
  5. The Learner Dashboard appears. From this window, you can access previous trainings, search for and enroll in the appropriate training sessions, and review your transcript. 
  6. To locate the appropriate courses, search using “TPT” or the course name from the table above in the search bar at the top of the window or by opening the Course Catalog tile. 
  7. Click Choose Session for each course you need to complete, then enroll in the session that best fits your schedule.  
  8. You will receive an email confirmation regarding the success of your enrollment. Additionally, you will receive a Microsoft Teams calendar event for each session.  
  9. On the day of the training, access the training via one of the following methods: 
    • Access the Teams Meeting hyperlink from the course confirmation email. 
    • Click the Microsoft Teams meeting hyperlink within the Outlook/Teams calendar event. 
    • Access My Courses in the LMS and click the appropriate Microsoft Teams meeting hyperlink. 

Do not forward meeting invitations to other attendees. Each participant must register through the LMS to receive course access

Chapter I, Section 4 requires that providers be “appropriately licensed, accredited, certified, and/or registered in the state where the member is located during the provision of the telehealth service.”

Annual Tea Celebrating Deaf Culture to Take Place September 17

The 35th annual tea and awards presentation will take place from 2 to 4 p.m. in the Hall of Flags

AUGUSTA, MAINE -In celebration of Deaf culture and the heritage of AmericanSign Language (ASL), as well as Deaf literature, art and folklore, Governor Janet Mills has issued a proclamation designating the week of Sept. 20-26, 2026, as Deaf Culture Week.

To kick off the week, the Commission for the Deaf, Hard of Hearing and Late Deafened will hold its 35th Annual Tea in Celebration of Deaf Culture Week on Sept. 17, from 2 to 4 p.m. at the Hall of Flags in the State House in Augusta. The event is open to the public.

Clayton Marr III will give the keynote address. Marr grew up in Westbrook and currently lives in Knoxville, Tenn. where he is the student activity coordinator for the Tennessee Schools for the Deaf. He works with Deaf students to support their academic success, personal growth, and independence.

"Maine's Deaf community has enriched our state for generations through its language, culture, traditions and contributions. I've proudly declared September 20-26 as Deaf Culture Week in celebration of that heritage and the Deaf and hard-of-hearing Mainers who make our state a better place," said Governor Mills.

"The Maine Department of Labor is proud to support the Commission for the Deaf, Hard of Hearing and Late Deafened and this 35th annual celebration of Deaf culture. I encourage Maine employers to harness the many skills and experiences of people with disabilities. DOL's Bureau of Rehabilitation Services is ready to assist workers and employers with vocational rehabilitation, training and support," said Commissioner Laura Fortman.

This year, the Commission will present seven awards to eight individuals and organizations that have contributed to Deaf culture in Maine.

Awards and their recipients are:

Promoting American Sign Language, Deaf Culture and Deaf People Award Lisa Penney, Donna Van Horn

Citizenship Youth Award Gavin Phelan

Ginny Hewes Advocate for the Needs of the Deaf Community Award Jennifer McCann, LCSW

Outstanding Citizenship Award Andrew Blethen

Outstanding Commendation Award Immigrant Legal Advocacy Project (ILAP)

Dr. Toni H. Rees Interpreter Award Cid Pollard

Clifton F. Rodgers Outstanding Service to the Deaf Community Award Sammy Hargis

The Division of the Deaf, Hard of Hearing and Late Deafened, within the Bureau of Rehabilitation Services in the Maine Department of Labor, works to promote full access to employment, independence and community integration for people who are deaf or hard of hearing.

By strengthening pre-apprenticeship programs and giving employers the guidance and tools necessary to funnel younger workers into registered apprenticeship programs, the Trump Administration is ensuring the American workforce gains and maintains the skills necessary to build the modern and future economy. ETA also issued Circular 2026-04, informing employers that sponsor registered apprentices how to obtain money made available through the new Workforce Pell Grant, created by the Working Families Tax Cuts Act. Maine Wasted Food Prevention Week - September 28 through October 4
item.description: WHEREAS , food is one of Maine’s most valuable resources and is essential for the health and nutrition of all our 1.4 million residents; and WHEREAS , nearly 40 percent of food produced in Maine is never eaten – over 361,000 tons annually – primarily ending up in landfills where it produces dangerous methane gas which is 28 times more potent than carbon dioxide and a major contributor to climate change; and WHEREAS , Maine people can save money by preventing wasted food, with the average Maine family spending nearly $3,000 annually on food that is thrown away; and WHEREAS , over 80 percent of consumers misunderstand food date labels causing large amounts of perfectly good food to be thrown away in homes, businesses, and even food pantries; and WHEREAS , Maine communities can substantially reduce their waste disposal costs by preventing wasted food since food is the single largest municipal solid waste component; and WHEREAS , Maine K-12 schools have a special role in educating our next generation to reduce, recover, and recycle the estimated 7 million pounds of school food wasted annually; and WHEREAS , we can help our farmers, strengthen our local food systems, and conserve our natural resources – water, air, energy, and land – by valuing Maine food and composting food scraps instead of wasting it as trash; NOW THEREFORE , be it resolved that I, Janet T. Mills, Governor of the State of Maine, do hereby proclaim the week of September 28-October 4, 2026, as Maine Wasted Food Prevention Week and I encourage all Maine people to become aware of the wasted food in our homes, schools and all around us, and to commit to stop throwing food away. In testimony whereof, I have caused the Great Seal of the State to be hereunto affixed GIVEN under my hand at Augusta this second day of September Two Thousand Twenty-Six

WHEREAS, food is one of Maine’s most valuable resources and is essential for the health and nutrition of all our 1.4 million residents; and

WHEREAS, nearly 40 percent of food produced in Maine is never eaten – over 361,000 tons annually – primarily ending up in landfills where it produces dangerous methane gas which is 28 times more potent than carbon dioxide and a major contributor to climate change; and

WHEREAS, Maine people can save money by preventing wasted food, with the average Maine family spending nearly $3,000 annually on food that is thrown away; and

WHEREAS, over 80 percent of consumers misunderstand food date labels causing large amounts of perfectly good food to be thrown away in homes, businesses, and even food pantries; and

WHEREAS, Maine communities can substantially reduce their waste disposal costs by preventing wasted food since food is the single largest municipal solid waste component; and

WHEREAS, Maine K-12 schools have a special role in educating our next generation to reduce, recover, and recycle the estimated 7 million pounds of school food wasted annually; and

WHEREAS, we can help our farmers, strengthen our local food systems, and conserve our natural resources – water, air, energy, and land – by valuing Maine food and composting food scraps instead of wasting it as trash; 

NOW THEREFORE, be it resolved that I, Janet T. Mills, Governor of the State of Maine, do hereby proclaim the week of September 28-October 4, 2026, as

Maine Wasted Food Prevention Week

and I encourage all Maine people to become aware of the wasted food in our homes, schools and all around us, and to commit to stop throwing food away.

In testimony whereof, I have caused 
the Great Seal of the State to be 
hereunto affixed GIVEN under my 
hand at Augusta this second day 
of September Two Thousand Twenty-Six

Registration is Open for the 2026 MaineCare Provider Conference

Sep 10, 2026

Join colleagues from across Maine for the inaugural 2026 MaineCare Provider Conference—a dynamic day of learning, collaboration, and connection. Centered on the theme "Stronger Together: Navigating Change Through Collaboration," this conference brings together providers from across the MaineCare community to share innovative practices, explore emerging challenges, and strengthen partnerships that improve care for the people we serve. 

This conference is made possible through support from Maine's Rural Health Transformation Program (RHTP), a federal initiative that helps strengthen rural healthcare by improving access to care, supporting the healthcare workforce, modernizing healthcare systems, and advancing innovative models of care across the state. The conference reflects these goals by creating opportunities for providers to learn from one another, build stronger partnerships, and share strategies that improve care for MaineCare members. 

Designed for professionals across primary care, behavioral health, oral health, community support services, and other disciplines, the conference features interactive presentations, practical strategies, and real-world solutions that participants can immediately apply in their work. Whether you're looking to expand your knowledge, exchange ideas with peers, or build new connections across Maine's healthcare and social service systems, this conference offers valuable opportunities to learn from one another and shape the future of care. 

The conference welcomes participants in all roles with MaineCare provider organizations, including: 

  • Clinicians 
  • Administrators 
  • Care coordinators 
  • Program staff 
  • Quality improvement professionals 
  • Other team members who support MaineCare members 

Together, we'll explore approaches that strengthen the healthcare workforce, improve access to care, enhance member engagement, and support better health outcomes for MaineCare members across the state. 

Provider Conference Details 

Date: October 27, 2026 

Time: 9:00 AM – 3:00 PM (Registration, Poster Session, and Networking time begins at 8:00 AM) 

Place: Augusta Civic Center, Community Drive, Augusta, ME 

Cost: Free!  

Space is limited, so register now!  

Some Providers Are Required to Participate – See the Special Code 

If you are a Delivery System Reform Unit (DSRU) provider including: 

  • Behavioral Health Homes 
  • Certified Community Behavioral Health Clinics 
  • Community Care Teams 
  • MaineMOM 
  • Opioid Health Homes 
  • Primary Care Plus 

MaineCare policy requires at least one member of your care team to attend this department-sponsored learning activity.  

The registration code specifically designated for DSRU providers to help account for required participation is DSRUPROVIDER. Click the “reserve a spot” button on the registration page, and enter this code into the promo code box, to ensure you can access the reserved DSRU tickets. 

For questions about this conference, please contact MaineCare’s communication team.

Attention Trading Partners: Training for New MaineCare Partner Portal

Sep 14, 2026

We have previously shared that a refreshed and upgraded MIHMS, with a new “MaineCare Partner Portal,” is coming in October 2026. This will replace the current HealthPAS Online Portal. We are now inviting trading partners to register for training that began September 8, 2026 to help you prepare for the transition to the new portal. Trading partners include providers, billing agents, health plans, clearinghouses, and business associates. Trading partners have an important role to play in supporting a smooth transition and uninterrupted access to the portal after go-live. 

Gainwell Technologies will be leading live virtual instructor-led training sessions. These courses will provide the knowledge and skills needed to navigate the new portal, complete daily business functions, and use new portal features. Training demonstrations, materials, and supporting resources will help participants prepare for a successful transition. 

Steps you need to take to attend training 

  • Review the available training topics listed below and identify the sessions that align with your role and responsibilities. 
  • Use the LMS registration (instructions below) to create an account, access the training catalog, and enroll in applicable sessions. 
  • Contact Gainwell (instructions below) if you need assistance. 
  • Recorded sessions and other training materials will be available in the LMS after training sessions for ongoing reference. 

MaineCare Partner Portal Training Sessions 

Course Name 

Description 

ME - TPT - Migrated Trading Partner Log In and Account Maintenance Training (ILC) 

Learn how to complete first-time login activities, configure multi-factor authentication (MFA), manage user accounts and permissions, perform account maintenance activities, and understand electronic data interchange (EDI) certification requirements and status monitoring. This course is only for Admin (R7) users. 

ME - TPT - Trading Partner Registration and Account Maintenance Training (ILC) 

Learn how to register a new Trading Partner account, complete account activation, manage users and permissions, associate providers and billing agents, navigate the portal, and maintain account information.  

ME - TPT - Authorization, Referrals and Certifications Training (ILC) 

Learn how to submit and manage authorizations, process referrals, monitor certification requests and statuses, and access related portal functionality. 

ME - TPT - Dental Claim Entry & Claim Management Training (ILC) 

Learn how to submit dental claims, monitor claim processing and status, and navigate claim-related portal functions. 

ME - TPT - Institutional Claim Entry & Claim Management Training (ILC) 

Learn how to submit institutional claims, monitor claim processing and status, and navigate claim-related portal functions. 

ME - TPT - Professional Claim Entry & Claim Management Training (ILC) 

Learn how to submit professional claims, monitor claim status, review payment information, access remittance advice, and complete related claim activities. 

ME - TPT - MaineCare Partner Public Portal Training (ILC) 

Learn about publicly available portal functionality, portal resources and reference materials, secure messaging, Trading Partner tools, and available resources. 

LMS Access and Course Registration Instructions 

Use the following steps to register for MaineCare Partner Portal training. Multiple sessions are available for each course to allow for scheduling flexibility. 

  1. Go to the LMS registration site: https://mmislearningcenter.myabsorb.com/#/login. 
  2. Sign in using your existing account or click Sign Up on the right side of the window to create a new account. 
  3. If you need a new account, enter the enrollment key: De8pO9CBYXYB-aOCY8qp on the Sign Up window. 
  4. Complete the required registration information to create your account. Note: You can enter your workplace address. 
  5. The Learner Dashboard appears. From this window, you can access previous trainings, search for and enroll in the appropriate training sessions, and review your transcript. 
  6. To locate the appropriate courses, search using “TPT” or the course name from the table above in the search bar at the top of the window or by opening the Course Catalog tile. 
  7. Click Choose Session for each course you need to complete, then enroll in the session that best fits your schedule.  
  8. You will receive an email confirmation regarding the success of your enrollment. Additionally, you will receive a Microsoft Teams calendar event for each session.  
  9. On the day of the training, access the training via one of the following methods: 
    • Access the Teams Meeting hyperlink from the course confirmation email. 
    • Click the Microsoft Teams meeting hyperlink within the Outlook/Teams calendar event. 
    • Access My Courses in the LMS and click the appropriate Microsoft Teams meeting hyperlink.

Attention Trading Partners: MIHMS Upgrade October Payment Cycle Changes and System Access Limitations

Sep 14, 2026

As previously communicated, the Office of MaineCare Services (OMS) is preparing to launch an upgraded version of MIHMS, MaineCare’s claims processing system. The upgrade is currently scheduled to go live on October 10, 2026. To support a smooth transition, OMS must implement temporary system access limitations and adjustments to payment cycles in October.  

From Friday, October 2 at 8:00 PM until Monday, October 12 at 8:00 AM, MIHMS will be in a “data freeze” while OMS completes final system readiness and transition activities. 

Please note that we have updated the FAQ previously shared, as of September 14, 2026. 

Changes to October payment cycles:

OMS may take up to 30 days to process and pay a claim, depending on any edits or issues that may cause the claim to pend for manual review, as well as other processing requirements that may require the full 30-day timeframe. 

Preparing for the changes to October payment cycles: 

The HealthPAS Online Portal has returned to its previous regular operating hours. Providers again have 24/7 access to the portal, for additional flexibility and time to submit claims outside of standard business hours.   

We strongly encourage providers to submit claims approaching timely filing limits in the next few weeks to avoid potential submission delays. The planned data freeze does not modify existing Medicaid timely filing requirements. Providers remain responsible for ensuring claims are submitted within the established timely filing guidelines.

Other system access limitations:   

Providers can find other expected impacts of the data freeze in this FAQ. We have updated the FAQ as of September 14, 2026. Topics include: 

  • HealthPAS Online Portal, including impacts on submitting claims, submitting prior authorizations, and checking member eligibility 
  • Provider Enrollment Application (PEA) 
  • Value-Based Purchasing Management System (VMS) Portal 
  • Paper & fax document submissions 
  • Provider Services & Member Services call centers 
  • Value Added Network (VAN) Trading Partners 
  • Prior authorizations for prescriptions and behavioral health services 
  • Electronic Visit Verification (EVV) 
  • Secure File Transfer Protocol (SFTP) 

You can also check the OMS Provider Resources webpage, in the first box of information called “Health PAS Online Portal,” for the most recent information about the upgrade.   

For questions or clarifications, please contact Provider Services at 1-866-690-5585. Please note, Provider Services does not have additional information beyond what is shared in this message and in the FAQ linked above.

item.description: CHICAGO – The U.S. Department of Labor has cited a Calumet City-based residential construction and carpentry employer after two separate investigations into its continued failure to provide fall protection for workers. The department’s Occupational Safety and Health Administration investigated two worksites operated by Martin Araujo – doing business as Araujo Construction Corp. – and found that carpenters and general construction laborers were installing roof rafters and roof sheeting without fall protection, exposing them to falls of up to 25 feet. OSHA cited Araujo Construction with two willful violations for not providing fall protection, while working from heights during residential construction at the two worksites. OSHA also cited the employer with nine repeat safety violations for failing to provide head and eye protection, lacking handrails on stairways, and failing to make sure ladders extended three feet above access areas. Additionally, OSHA issued a serious violation to Araujo Construction for not having safe access to a platform, and an other-than-serious violation for lacking training certifications. OSHA proposed $265,868 in combined penalties.Martin Araujo has 15 business days from receipt of its citations and penalties to comply, request an informal conference with OSHA’s area director, or contest the findings before the independent Occupational Safety and Health Review Commission. Please check the OSHA establishment search page periodically for any changes in the inspection or penalty status. Under the Occupational Safety and Health Act of 1970, employers are responsible for providing safe and healthful workplaces for their employees. OSHA’s role is to ensure these conditions for America’s working men and women by setting and enforcing standards, and providing training, education and assistance. See OSHA’s website for more information.

Sep 16, 2026

The Maine Department of Health and Human Services’ Center for Disease Control and Prevention (Maine CDC) is reporting a case of measles in Maine; the first case in the state since five cases were confirmed in February of this year. The Maine CDC confirmed the latest case on September 15, 2026. According to the U.S. Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (U.S. CDC), as of September 11, there were 3,294 confirmed measles cases reported nationwide in 2026.

The individual is an unvaccinated adult from Somerset County. The Maine CDC is working with the facility where potential exposure occurred and is working with them to inform potentially exposed individuals.

Individuals who were at the following location* during the timeframe listed below were potentially exposed to measles and should take precautions and should watch for symptoms for 21 days after September 12:

Location

Date

Time

MaineGeneral Express Care, Waterville 211 Main Street, Waterville, ME

September 12, 2026

8am-11am

*Subject to change as the investigation continues

Measles is a highly contagious viral disease. If one person has measles, 90% of the people close to that person who are not immune will become infected. Symptoms of measles include:

  • Fever
  • Cough
  • Runny nose
  • Red, watery eyes
  • Rash that spreads from the head down.

Individuals who develop symptoms should contact their health care provider for instructions before going to the provider’s office or hospital. This will help prevent the spread of further infection. If symptoms are consistent with measles, a health care professional may test to determine a measles infection.

Measles can cause severe sickness including pneumonia, encephalitis (brain swelling), and death. An infected person spreads measles through coughs or sneezes. Once infected, a person is contagious from four days before their rash starts through four days afterwards. The virus remains alive for up to two hours on surfaces and in the air. The period from exposure to onset of symptoms is typically 10 to 14 days, but can be longer.

The measles, mumps, and rubella (MMR) vaccine is the best prevention for measles. Individuals who:   

  • have been potentially exposed should review their vaccine history and watch for symptoms.
  • are not immunized or do not know their measles immunization status should get vaccinated.
  • develop symptoms should contact their health provider for instructions before going to the provider’s office or hospital. This will help prevent the spread of further infection.

Recommendations: 

  • Children – Identify and vaccinate children who are not up to date with their MMR vaccines. All children should receive two doses of MMR vaccine. A health care professional should administer the first dose to children at 12 to 15 months old and the second at 4 to 6 years old.
    • Children 6 to 11 months old who will be traveling internationally or domestically to a region with a known active measles outbreak should receive one dose of MMR vaccine, per the Maine CDC’s expanded recommendations for those traveling to a destination with a known outbreak. This dose is not considered part of the routine two-dose series starting at age 12 months.  
  • Adults – All adults should have proof of immunity to measles. Acceptable proof includes one of the following:
    • written documentation of vaccination
    • laboratory evidence of immunity
    • birth before 1957
    • or laboratory confirmation of disease
    • individuals who received a measles vaccine between 1963 to 1967 are encouraged to speak with their doctor to determine if additional vaccination is needed. Those known to have received an inactivated dose measles vaccine should receive a single dose of MMR. Five percent of people who received measles vaccine between 1963 and 1967 received an inactivated vaccine.

For adults with no evidence of immunity to measles, the U.S. CDC recommends one dose of MMR vaccine as soon as possible. Adults who are traveling domestically or internationally to a region known to have an active measles outbreak should receive two doses of the vaccine. Pregnant women should not receive any live virus vaccine during pregnancy, including MMR.

Vaccination Information:

  • Two doses of MMR vaccine are about 97% effective at preventing measles; one dose is about 93% effective.
  • The U.S. CDC considers people who received two doses of MMR vaccine as a child protected for life. 
  • Some people exposed to the virus may still get measles even if they got the MMR vaccine. In this case, they are more likely to have a milder illness and are also less likely to spread the disease to other people.

For More Information:

  • The Maine CDC’s measles webpage: http://www.maine.gov/dhhs/measles
  • The U.S. CDC’s measles webpage: http://www.cdc.gov/measles/index.html
  • The Maine Immunization Program webpage: https://www.maine.gov/dhhs/mecdc/infectious-disease/immunization/

The Employment Situation in Maine - August 2026

September 18, 2026

Released: 10 a.m. Friday, September 18, 2026

Contact: Mark McInerney, (207) 620-0197

The 3.2 unemployment rate in August changed little from July. Nonfarm wage and salary jobs have remained within a narrow range for 28 consecutive months.

Seasonally Adjusted Statewide Labor Force Estimates

The 3.2 percent unemployment rate changed little from recent months. Unemployment rates have remained within a narrow range between 3.1 and 3.3 percent for 24 consecutive months. Unemployment has been below 4 percent for 56 months, the longest duration on record. Maine's unemployment rate has been below the U.S. average for more than 18 years, and remains below the long-term average of 5.4 percent for the state since 1976. Unemployment averaged 4.1 percent for New England and 4.1 percent for the U.S. in the month.

The labor force participation rate averaged 58.8 percent over the last three months, lower than during the three months through May. A decreasing employment-to-population ratio in the three months through August is the primary reason for lower rates of labor force participation.

Seasonally Adjusted Statewide Nonfarm Jobs Estimates

Preliminary seasonally adjusted estimates indicate that in August, nonfarm wage and salary jobs were little changed from July. Employment levels were stable in every sector.

Job estimates have stayed within a narrow range near 660,000 for 28 consecutive months (estimates ranging less than 0.5 percent higher or lower each month). Over the last year, job increases in the health care and social assistance, and retail trade sectors were offset by modest decreases across several sectors.

Not Seasonally Adjusted County and Metro Area Labor Force Estimates

On a not seasonally adjusted basis, the statewide unemployment rate was 3.1 percent. Rates were at least 0.3 percentage points higher than that in seven counties, at least 0.3 points lower than that in four, and close to the average in five. Rates were lowest in the coastal counties and highest along the northern rim of the state.

Among the three metro areas, unemployment was below the statewide average in Portland-S. Portland, and close to the average in Bangor and Lewiston-Auburn.

Not Seasonally Adjusted Statewide and Metro Area Hours and Earnings Estimates

The private sector workweek averaged 33.5 hours and earnings averaged $33.77 per hour in August. Average hours changed little, and hourly earnings increased 4.2 percent from one year ago. The workweek was longest in the construction and manufacturing sectors and shortest in the leisure and hospitality sector. Earnings were highest in professional and business services and lowest in leisure and hospitality. Hourly earnings were above the statewide average in Portland-S. Portland and below it in the Bangor and Lewiston-Auburn metros.

Media Contact: Autumn Mahoney, Communications Specialist media.dol@maine.gov

AUGUSTA - The Maine Department of Labor announced today that, effective January 1, 2027, the state minimum wage will increase from $15.10 to $15.70 per hour, based on data recently made available by the U.S. Department of Labor's Bureau of Labor Statistics. MDOL is required under Maine law (Maine statute Title 26, chapter 7, section 664) to make annual adjustments to the minimum wage based on the cost-of-living index (CPI-W) for the Northeast Region, after Maine voters amended the law by referendum in 2016. Between August 2025 and August 2026, there was a 4.1 percent increase in the CPI-W.

According to the U.S. Department of Labor's Bureau of Labor Statistics Current Population Survey for 2025, there were 28,000 hourly workers who were paid less than $15.00 per hour. These workers represent about four percent of all wage and salary workers (both paid at hourly rates and not paid at hourly rates) and about eight percent of wage and salary workers who are paid at hourly rates.

Agricultural workers in Maine are also entitled to the state minimum wage, after the Legislature enacted and Governor Mills signed "An Act to Establish a State Minimum Hourly Wage for Agricultural Workers" in 2025.

The "tip wage," or service employee minimum wage, will increase from $7.55 to $7.85 per hour. This means that service employees must receive a direct cash wage of at least $7.85 per hour from the employer. The employer must be able to show that the employee receives at least the minimum wage of $15.70 per hour when the direct wage and tips are combined at the end of the week. The amount of tips necessary to qualify as a service employee will increase from $191 to $199 per month.

The minimum salary threshold for exempting a worker from overtime pay must exceed 3,000 times the State's minimum wage or the annualized rate established by the U.S. Department of Labor, whichever is higher. Starting January 1, 2027, the new minimum salary threshold for salaried workers exempt from overtime will be $905.79 per week, or $47,101.08 per year. This is only one of the factors used in determining whether a worker is exempt from overtime pay under federal or state law. An individual can earn more than the minimum salary threshold and still be eligible for overtime. The duties of each worker must be considered as part of this analysis.

Employers can download the required minimum wage poster at no cost on the Department's website.

The minimum wage and overtime law can be found here.
